title: 0605 item 9: the TIN branch code prints three compartments, BIR's own runtime declares five

subject.description: The fourth (branch-code) group of the item-9 'Taxpayer Identification No.' comb chain on page 1. The chain prints 30.24-68.88 / 81.48-121.56 / 134.16-172.68 / 183.00-223.92, separated by three grey (gray 0.7529) filled-and-stroked boxes 12.60 / 12.60 / 10.32pt wide. The caption on this sheet is spelled out as 'Taxpayer Identification No.', not 'TIN'. After the 2026-08-17 sitting the whole chain (not only this box) is reflowed to even 3-3-3-5 inside the original outer span; this printed box remains the PDF identity of the branch group.

reason: BIR's 1999 artwork for 0605 is CORRECT and OUT OF DATE. It prints three compartments for the TIN branch code — and, unlike 2550M, pre-prints nothing in them. BIR's own eBIRForms client, whose runtime this repository has harvested, declares that same field with max_length 5. No rule can derive 'BIR widened this field after 1999' from 1999 ink, which is precisely why this is a stage-2 correction and not a stage-1 producer bug (ARCHITECTURE.md, 'What belongs in which stage').

corpus_context.measured_on: 2026-08-08 for the 53-bundle census; 2026-08-17 for this bundle's own by-hand measurement
corpus_context.summary: Of 53 bundles, the census measured 39 printing 3+3+3+5, three printing 3+3+3+3 (2550M Feb 2007, 2551M 2002, 2553 1999), one printing 3+3+3+4 (1600WP 2010), and ten not measurable by that method. 0605-1999 is one of those ten. Measured by hand from the pinned PDF for this record, it prints 3+3+3+3 — a fourth bundle in that class, and one whose branch code BIR's own runtime declares at max_length 5. It is therefore one of the writable-3 sites: a box the taxpayer can type three characters into for a field the Bureau's client accepts five for.
corpus_context.census_pin_not_edited: tools/formgen/corrections/evidence/tin-branch-census-20260808.json still records 0605-1999 as {"measured": false}. That is what its method measured and the pin stays as it is; the hand measurement lives here, with its two reasons for the method's miss, so a reader can see the difference rather than a rewritten number.
corpus_context.this_record_corrects_one_site_only: 0605-1999 page 1 item 9. The other 3+3+3+3 bundles, the 3+3+3+4 bundle and the nine remaining not-measurable bundles each need their own record, evidence and review.
corpus_context.declaration_is_not_uniform: The HTA does not declare 5 everywhere: rules/forms/1601c-v2018/fields.json declares frm1601c:txtBranchCode max_length 3 while the 1601C artwork prints 5, and 1701MS / 1701Q / 2550Q declare 3 for their page-1 branch fields. So 'the HTA always says 5' is false and must not be used as a general rule. This record rests on 0605's own declared value, not on a corpus-wide assumption.

filing_safety.harm: The payment is credited to the wrong branch. A TIN's branch code identifies the establishment a remittance belongs to, and 0605 is the payment form — it is how a taxpayer pays a deficiency, a penalty, a compromise, an instalment or the annual registration fee. If the branch code cannot be entered, the payment lands on branch 000, the head office, while the branch that owes the amount shows nothing paid and stays open on the Bureau's books.
filing_safety.who_is_affected: Every 0605 filer whose branch code is not three digits, i.e. any registered branch numbered above 999 (four or five digits). They have no way to enter it on today's form at all.
filing_safety.today: Three compartments, nothing pre-printed, all three typeable: the filer can enter a three-digit code and can enter nothing longer.
filing_safety.after: Five compartments over the same emitted box; a four- or five-digit branch code becomes enterable, and the emitted value can carry the five characters BIR's own client accepts for frm0605:txtBranchCode.
